title: Optimizing Calibration by Gaining Aware of Prediction Correctness

contributions.purpose: Fix the intrinsic limitation of CE/MSE post-hoc calibration losses, which give high confidence to narrowly misclassified samples, by deriving a calibration objective directly from the aim of calibration.
contributions.mechanism: Derive the discretized calibration error and translate it into a Correctness-Aware (CA) loss: enforce high confidence (~1) on correctly classified samples and low confidence (~1/C) on wrongly classified ones, reducing overlap of confidence between correct and incorrect predictions.
contributions.evaluation: Trained on the ImageNet-Val calibration set with 10 Timm classifiers; competitive ECE/BS/KS/AUROC vs SOTA calibrators on IND (ImageNet-Val) and OOD (ImageNet-A/R/S, ObjectNet) test sets.
contributions.domain: Model calibration / uncertainty in image classification
contributions.source_quote: we propose a new post-hoc calibration objective derived from the aim of calibration ... asks that the calibrator decrease model confidence on wrongly predicted samples and increase confidence on correctly predicted samples.

contributions.purpose: Estimate prediction correctness for an isolated individual test sample, which a single sample cannot indicate on its own.
contributions.mechanism: Use softmax prediction scores of transformed versions of the original image (rotated, greyscaled, color-jittered) as calibrator inputs; consistency among transformed predictions signals correctness.
contributions.evaluation: Enables calibrator trained on IND validation set to be applied directly to individual test samples; qualitative demonstration of better separation of correct vs incorrect samples by calibrated confidence.
contributions.domain: Model calibration / uncertainty in image classification
contributions.source_quote: To indicate prediction correctness, we use the softmax prediction scores of transformed versions of the original image as calibrator inputs.

contributions.purpose: Explain why standard calibration losses fail on certain samples.
contributions.mechanism: Diagnostic analysis of CE and MSE losses relative to the newly derived calibration goal.
contributions.evaluation: Finding: CE and MSE deviate from the calibration aim on 'narrowly wrong' predictions, which take up 2%-8% of the ImageNet validation calibration set.
contributions.source_quote: We diagnose commonly used calibration loss functions including the CE and MSE loss: they are often limited under test samples of certain characteristics.

self_declared_provenance.quote: This paper identifies inherent problems with MLE for calibration and derives a new loss function that better aligns with calibration goal.
In comparison, our calibrator is trained on the IND validation set only, and does not need test batches for update, but still demonstrates improved and competitive OOD calibration performance.

notes: Authors describe results only as 'competitive' with SOTA (not clearly superior) on IND, and 'superior to and on par with state of the art on OOD and IND test sets, respectively' - i.e., roughly comparable, a hedged/tie result on IND. ICLR 2025 reject.
